name: Capricornus
introduction: is the Sea-Goat, a creature with the front of a goat and the tail of a fish, inherited from Babylonian astronomy more than 3,000 years ago. It is the smallest zodiac constellation, a faint triangle best seen on southern winter and northern late-summer evenings. About 2,000 years ago, the Sun stood here at the December solstice, which gave the Tropic of Capricorn its name.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: At its western end, sharp eyes can split Algedi into two stars, [Algedi](hip:100064) and Prima Giedi. They are not related: one lies about 110 light-years away, the other more than five times farther.
In 1846, Johann Galle found the planet Neptune in Capricornus, close to the position predicted by Urbain Le Verrier from the way it pulled on Uranus.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Deneb Algedi](hip:107556), the brightest star, marks the sea-goat’s tail. It is an eclipsing binary only 39 light-years away. [Dabih](hip:100345) is a multiple system with a golden giant, and [Nashira](hip:106985) completes the tail.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The globular cluster M30 has a dense core in which stars crowd extremely close together. Each summer, the slow, bright Alpha Capricornid meteors radiate from Capricornus.
